The optical system is configured with four lens groups arranged in sequence from the object side toward the image side. These include a first lens group having positive refractive power, an intermediate lens group having negative refractive power, a focusing lens group having positive refractive power, and an image-side lens group also having positive refractive power.

In this configuration, focusing is performed by moving the positive focusing lens group along the optical axis. Because the focusing function is assigned to this positive lens group, the amount of movement required for focus adjustment can be controlled efficiently. In addition, the focusing lens group can be made relatively lightweight, which is advantageous for achieving rapid and accurate focusing operation.

During magnification changes, the axial distances between adjacent lens groups are varied. By changing these intervals, the optical system can adjust magnification while maintaining favorable correction of aberrations across the zoom range. This arrangement enables the system to provide stable imaging performance from one magnification state to another.

The optical system is further designed to satisfy a predetermined conditional expression. By meeting this condition, the balance of refractive power, lens group spacing, and aberration correction can be optimized. As a result, the optical system achieves excellent optical performance while also maintaining a compact and efficient focusing structure.

Accordingly, the design provides both high image quality and high-speed focusing capability. The lightweight positive focusing lens group reduces the load on the focusing drive mechanism, allowing fast response during autofocus operation, while the overall lens group arrangement supports superior optical performance throughout focusing and magnification changes.
outputs.L4:
A variable magnification optical system is provided which is capable of changing its focal length while maintaining excellent imaging performance over the entire zoom range. The optical system includes, in order from an object side to an image side, four lens groups having predetermined refractive powers, including at least one lens group having positive refractive power and at least one lens group having negative refractive power. During magnification, the distances between adjacent lens groups are varied so that the overall focal length of the optical system changes from a wide-angle end to a telephoto end. In addition, focusing is performed by moving a designated focusing lens group along the optical axis.

The focusing lens group is configured so as to have a reduced weight while still contributing effectively to correction of aberrations. By selecting the refractive powers of the four lens groups, the movement amounts of the lens groups during magnification, and the position and optical power of the focusing lens group so as to satisfy a predetermined conditional expression, the system suppresses variations in aberrations caused by zooming and focusing. As a result, the optical system can provide high resolution, low distortion, and stable image quality from the center of the image field to the peripheral region.

Because the focusing operation is carried out by a lightweight lens group, the load on the focus driving mechanism is reduced. This enables rapid and accurate focus adjustment, making the optical system suitable for applications requiring high-speed autofocus, such as interchangeable camera lenses, video cameras, and imaging devices used for moving subjects. At the same time, the four-group zoom configuration allows the lens barrel to be made compact while ensuring a desirable zoom ratio and high optical performance.

Thus, the variable magnification optical system achieves both excellent optical performance and improved focusing responsiveness. The arrangement of positive and negative lens groups, the controlled variation of intergroup spacing during zooming, and the satisfaction of the specified optical condition collectively make it possible to reduce the weight of the focusing lens group without sacrificing image quality.

counterfactuals.output:
A variable magnification optical system includes, in order from an object side to an image side, a first lens group G1 having positive refractive power, a second lens group G2 having negative refractive power, a third lens group G3 having positive refractive power, and a fourth lens group G4 having positive refractive power. During zooming from a wide-angle end to a telephoto end, at least one of the axial distances between adjacent lens groups changes, including a change in a distance between G1 and G2 and a change in a distance between G2 and G3, thereby varying magnification. The third lens group G3 is movable along an optical axis for focusing from an infinity object distance to a short object distance. The optical system satisfies the following conditional expression:

\[
0.20 < \frac{f_3}{f_T} < 0.80
\]

where \(f_3\) denotes a focal length of the third lens group G3, and \(f_T\) denotes a focal length of the entire optical system at the telephoto end. By using the positive third lens group as a focusing group while controlling the refractive power relationship, high-speed focusing, compactness, and favorable aberration correction over the entire zoom range are achieved.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in patent terminology, a variable magnification optical system including four lens groups G1, G2, G3, and G4, their signs and positions, how spacing changes during zooming, and the resulting advantages.
counterfactuals.output:
A variable magnification optical system is configured, in order from an object side toward an image side, to include a first lens group G1 having positive refractive power, a second lens group G2 having negative refractive power, a third lens group G3 having positive refractive power, and a fourth lens group G4 having positive refractive power.

During zooming from a wide-angle end state to a telephoto end state, at least one of the lens groups is moved along an optical axis so that an axial air separation between adjacent lens groups is varied. More specifically, the first lens group G1 is disposed closest to the object side and mainly contributes to light convergence and front-side aberration correction. The second lens group G2 is disposed on the image side of the first lens group G1 and functions as a variator group for changing magnification. The third lens group G3 is disposed on the image side of the second lens group G2 and functions as a compensator or relay group for correcting displacement of an image plane caused by magnification variation. The fourth lens group G4 is disposed closest to the image side and functions as an image-forming group, and may also be used for focusing.

In one embodiment, upon zooming from the wide-angle end to the telephoto end, a distance between the first lens group G1 and the second lens group G2 is increased, a distance between the second lens group G2 and the third lens group G3 is decreased, and a distance between the third lens group G3 and the fourth lens group G4 is varied so as to maintain the image plane substantially stationary. The first lens group G1 may move toward the object side, the second lens group G2 may move toward the image side or follow a nonlinear locus, the third lens group G3 may move so as to compensate for image-plane shift, and the fourth lens group G4 may remain fixed or may move slightly for focusing or aberration correction.

According to this configuration, a compact zoom optical system can be obtained while securing a high variable-magnification ratio. Since the negative second lens group G2 is used as a main variator and the positive third lens group G3 is used for compensation, variation of the back focal length and movement of the image plane during zooming can be effectively suppressed. Further, by arranging the lens groups in the order of positive, negative, positive, and positive refractive power, spherical aberration, coma, astigmatism, field curvature, and chromatic aberration can be favorably corrected over the entire zoom range. As a result, the optical system provides high imaging performance from the wide-angle end to the telephoto end, while allowing reduction in total lens length and suitability for use in compact imaging apparatuses such as digital cameras, video cameras, surveillance cameras, and mobile imaging devices.
